correctness.rationale: The supplied connected six-vertex graph, 0/2 BR and 1/3/4/5 imitators, strict opponent-coordinate payoffs and specified 10-switch word were independently recalculated from all integer edge payoffs. Each of ten updates changes the indicated bit, each imitation has exactly one maximum-earning neighbor and each BR improves strictly; after 10 switches the initial six-bit state is reached. Vertex 5 has an idle activation at that state; adding it at the start gives a repeating length-11 activation word visiting all six vertices each period. Thus deterministic fair non-equilibration is a complete finite existential proof for *neighbor-only* imitation, not an assertion about random schedules or own-payoff threshold rules.

The six-agent ten-switch certificate is a correct reproducible example but the source gives no mathematical need for exactly six agents, four imitators, two best responders, or ten switches, and explicitly disclaims minimality. A previously documented four-agent fair periodic orbit already refutes universal convergence on connected coordinating mixed networks, and the earlier formal orbit uses strict best-response moves and uniquely maximizing imitator neighbors on effective steps. Merely producing a larger, less sharp counterexample without a new natural invariant, threshold, minimality, robustness principle, or motivated constraint does not establish incremental mathematical value.
